title: Microsoft Edge: Select Password option in the right-click menu
summary: The briefing matches the roadmap and Microsoft's Beta Channel release notes. The policy paths, registry locations and corrected description of blocked domains are supported; searches found no dedicated Select Password switch, feature-specific licensing or Stable channel version.

claims.claim: Select Password appears in the context menu when users right-click a recognised username or password field.
claims.quote: When a user right-clicks a recognized username or password field, a new Select Password option appears in the context menu.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The option provides manual access to saved credentials when automatic password suggestions do not appear.
claims.quote: Users can now manually access saved credentials when password suggestions don't appear automatically.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The default state is on: the option arrives without administrator configuration.
claims.quote: When a user right-clicks a recognized username or password field, a new Select Password option appears in the context menu. ... No configuration is required, and existing password management policies continue to apply.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft says existing password management policies continue to apply to the option.
claims.quote: No configuration is required, and existing password management policies continue to apply.

claims.claim: Users with saved credentials can search them by domain or username.
claims.quote: From there, users with saved credentials can: ... Search saved credentials by domain or username

claims.claim: Users with saved credentials can fill credentials directly into the selected field.
claims.quote: Fill credentials directly into the selected field

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Viewing credential details requires completing OS authentication.
claims.quote: View credential details after completing OS authentication

claims.claim: Users can manage saved passwords through existing Edge Password Manager surfaces.
claims.quote: Manage saved passwords through existing Edge Password Manager surfaces

claims.claim: Roadmap item 570662 concerns Microsoft Edge's Select Password context-menu option.
claims.quote: "id": 570662, "title": "Microsoft Edge: Select Password from the context menu"

claims.claim: The roadmap modification timestamp is 2026-10-30T22:08:34.
The Learn entry describes the feature as available using the words 'Users can now', unlike the roadmap's In development status.
claims.quote: Users can now manually access saved credentials when password suggestions don't appear automatically.

claims.claim: At the time of writing, Microsoft Learn describes this option only in the Beta Channel release-notes entry.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Select Password" "Microsoft Edge" configuration documentation' and '"Microsoft Edge" "Select Password" "Stable"'; read results and opened Beta notes, Stable notes and Edge policy references. Only the Beta entry described this option.

claims.claim: The Select Password release-notes entry names no new data source.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Select Password" "Microsoft Edge" configuration documentation'; opened and read the complete Select Password Beta entry. It describes saved credentials and existing Password Manager surfaces, not a new data source.

claims.claim: The Select Password release-notes entry does not specify authentication before filling a field.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Select Password" "Microsoft Edge" configuration documentation'; read the complete Beta entry and PrimaryPasswordSetting reference. The entry specifies OS authentication for viewing details but not for filling.

claims.claim: The release-notes entry describes no automatic action by the new option.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Select Password" "Microsoft Edge" configuration documentation'; opened and read the complete Beta entry. It describes a user right-click and actions available from the menu, not an automatic action by this option.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The licensing model for this option is unknown because feature-specific licensing has not been published.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Edge 'Select Password' licensing price meter; Microsoft Edge browser password manager licensing prerequisites free cost license. Read results, Beta entry and Edge for Business overview/prerequisites; none names a licence covering this option.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Neither the roadmap record nor the option's release-notes entry names a licence, plan or meter.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Microsoft Edge" "Select Password" licensing price meter'; read the roadmap record and complete Select Password Beta entry. Neither names a licence, plan or meter for this option.

claims.claim: Microsoft has published no price for the Select Password option.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Microsoft Edge" "Select Password" licensing price meter' and Microsoft Edge browser password manager licensing prerequisites free cost license. Read results, Beta entry and Edge for Business overview; no price for this option appeared.

claims.claim: The release-notes entry names no role or licence prerequisite for users with saved credentials.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Select Password" "Microsoft Edge" configuration documentation' and '"Microsoft Edge" "Select Password" licensing price meter'; read the complete Beta entry. It says 'users with saved credentials' and names no role or licence.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated a Stable channel version for this option at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Microsoft Edge" "Select Password" "Stable"'; read results and searched the fetched Stable notes for 'Select Password' and 'context menu' with no matches. The matching feature entry is in Beta notes.

claims.claim: Group Policy exposes PasswordManagerEnabled at Administrative Templates > Microsoft Edge > Password manager and protection > Enable saving passwords to the password manager.
claims.quote: Group Policy (ADMX) info ... GP name: Enable saving passwords to the password manager ... GP path (Mandatory): Administrative Templates/Microsoft Edge/Password manager and protection

claims.claim: PasswordManagerEnabled uses the registry location SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge and value name PasswordManagerEnabled.
claims.quote: Registry settings ... Path (Mandatory): SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge ... Value name: PasswordManagerEnabled ... Value type: REG\_DWORD

claims.claim: PasswordManagerEnabled controls saving new passwords in Edge's password manager.
claims.quote: If you enable or don't configure this policy, users can save and add their passwords in Microsoft Edge. If you disable this policy, users can't save and add new passwords, but they can still use previously saved passwords.

claims.claim: Disabling PasswordManagerEnabled does not prevent use of previously saved passwords.
claims.quote: If you disable this policy, users can't save and add new passwords, but they can still use previously saved passwords.

claims.claim: PasswordManagerEnabled can govern individual user profiles.
claims.quote: Per Profile: Yes

claims.claim: PasswordManagerEnabled is not documented as governing the new Select Password option itself.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Microsoft Edge" "Select Password" "policy"'; read Beta notes, policy list and PasswordManagerEnabled. Its documented control is saving new passwords; previously saved passwords remain usable. No passage names it as governing the new option.

claims.claim: Group Policy exposes PasswordManagerBlocklist under Administrative Templates > Microsoft Edge > Password manager and protection with the printed Save and Fill setting label.
claims.quote: GP name: Configure the list of domains for which the password manager UI (Save and Fill) will be disabled ... GP path (Mandatory): Administrative Templates/Microsoft Edge/Password manager and protection

claims.claim: PasswordManagerBlocklist uses SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge\PasswordManagerBlocklist with numbered registry values 1, 2, 3.
claims.quote: Path (Mandatory): SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge\PasswordManagerBlocklist ... Value name: 1, 2, 3, ... ... Value type: List of REG\_SZ

claims.where: controls[1].governs, note; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: PasswordManagerBlocklist disables Save and Fill for configured domains, preventing password-manager use for those URLs.
claims.quote: This means that Save and Fill workflows are disabled, ensuring that passwords for those websites can't be saved or auto filled into web forms. ... In addition, users can't use password manager for those URLs.

claims.claim: PasswordManagerBlocklist is supported on Windows and macOS, not Android or iOS.
claims.quote: Windows: ≥ 99 ... macOS: ≥ 99 ... Android: Not supported ... iOS: Not supported

claims.claim: PasswordManagerBlocklist can govern individual user profiles.
claims.quote: Per Profile: Yes

claims.claim: Group Policy exposes PrimaryPasswordSetting under Administrative Templates > Microsoft Edge > Password manager and protection with the printed device-password autofill setting label.
claims.quote: GP name: Configures a setting that asks users to enter their device password while using password autofill ... GP path (Mandatory): Administrative Templates/Microsoft Edge/Password manager and protection

claims.claim: PrimaryPasswordSetting uses SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge and registry value name PrimaryPasswordSetting.
claims.quote: Path (Mandatory): SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge ... Value name: PrimaryPasswordSetting ... Value type: REG\_DWORD

claims.where: controls[2].governs, note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: PrimaryPasswordSetting set to WithDevicePassword requires device authentication before saved-password autofill.
claims.quote: If you set this policy to 'WithDevicePassword', users have to enter their device password (or preferred mode of authentication under Windows) to prove their identity before their password is autofilled.

claims.claim: PrimaryPasswordSetting is supported on Windows and macOS, not Android or iOS.
claims.quote: Windows: ≥ 93 ... macOS: ≥ 93 ... Android: Not supported ... iOS: Not supported

claims.claim: PrimaryPasswordSetting can govern individual user profiles.
claims.quote: Per Profile: Yes

claims.claim: Microsoft documents no dedicated setting to turn the Select Password option on or off on either the UI or automation surface.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Microsoft Edge" "Select Password" "policy"' and '"Select Password" "Microsoft Edge" configuration documentation'; opened Beta notes and Edge policy list, searching 'Select.?Password' and 'context menu'. No dedicated switch or registry policy appeared.

claims.claim: PasswordManagerEnabled is configurable through a macOS preference key.
claims.quote: Mac information and settings ... Preference Key name: PasswordManagerEnabled

claims.claim: PasswordManagerBlocklist is configurable through a macOS preference key.
claims.quote: Mac information and settings ... Preference Key name: PasswordManagerBlocklist

claims.claim: PrimaryPasswordSetting is configurable through a macOS preference key.
claims.quote: Mac information and settings ... Preference Key name: PrimaryPasswordSetting

claims.claim: The Select Password release-notes entry does not name which existing password management policies apply.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Microsoft Edge" "Select Password" "policy"'; read the complete Select Password Beta entry and all three cited policy references. The entry says 'existing password management policies continue to apply' without naming individual policies.
